A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SSR research and contain readable main text, equations, tables, figures, references, and Appendices A–C. Their shared structure and retained experiments support a reliable comparison despite substantive method revisions.

before.justification: v1 reports original recommendation and cold-start results on three Amazon datasets, component ablations, sensitivity experiments, and spectral representation analyses.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results in Tables 1–2, Figures 2–4, and Appendix C.

M1.justification: Sections 3.1–3.5 substantially revise the stated procedure: SBM targets encoder representations instead of predictions; G-HSNO replaces full-matrix CP kernels with diagonal mixing and replaces projected nonlinear gating with normalized reweighting; the objective gains kernel/filter regularization. v3 also introduces size-dependent Chebyshev filtering and masks that retain at least one band. The four-stage framework remains.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate Amazon Baby, Sports, and Clothing with the same multimodal recommendation tasks and cold-start scenarios. Appendix B.1 and Table 3 retain the same dataset populations and statistics; no additional domain or task is evaluated.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged within both reported comparisons: Table 1 retains its fourteen baselines, and Table 2 retains GRCN, BM3, LATTICE, FREEDOM, MMIL, and SMORE. Newly cited methods such as FITMM are not added to the evaluated comparisons.

E3.justification: Appendix B.4 extends the reported validation search over {0.0001, 0.001, 0.01, 0.1, 1.0} to the added regularization term. The chronological 80/10/10 split, negative sampling, full-ranking metrics, embedding size, batch size, and stopping rule remain unchanged. This documents a setting addition without establishing that experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: The component ablations, sensitivity curves for lambda, eta, and band count, t-SNE visualizations, modality-center distances, and cold-start gating analyses are retained. Figures 2–4 supply identical evidence, and no analysis of the newly added regularizer or filtering branch is reported.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, or significance-testing procedures. The retained claims of significant improvements and the gating-distribution plots introduce no change in statistical uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Appendix C.1 removes the specific eta approximately 10^-3 to 10^-2 recommendation, retaining only the qualitative statement about moderate contrastive regularization. All numerical entries in Tables 1–3 and all plotted results remain unchanged; no new benchmark outcome or performance gain between versions is reported.

T1.justification: The mathematical specification is substantially revised: Section 3.3 replaces the CP kernel definition with diagonal filters and softmax-normalized mixing, Eq. (7) changes aggregation, and Eq. (9) gains regularization. Section 3.1 also removes the sum-to-one gate constraint and the linearity-based fusion-order equivalence claim. The Laplacian/GFT and Appendix A definitions remain; no theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction redefine SBM's stated contribution from prediction consistency to representation consistency. The broader claims about the four-stage framework, low-rank spectral reasoning, and gains on sparse and cold-start recommendation remain unchanged.

C2.justification: v3 explicitly limits full eigendecomposition to small graphs and motivates approximation for scalability, normalization to prevent scale drift, and added regularization for training stability. These add substantive applicability and mechanism explanations. The empirical interpretations and Appendix C.4 limitations otherwise remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v3 supplies a code-repository location and additional implementation information about masking, scaling, spectral approximation, and regularization-weight selection. Important choices such as the numerical graph-size threshold and polynomial degree remain unspecified. Appendix B.4 still promises a future code/data release despite the abstract's availability statement; repository contents cannot be established from the PDFs.

R1.justification: v3 adds citations including FITMM, modal-aware bias constrained contrastive learning, MAESTRO, and several LLM/agent works, and replaces the survey cited as reference 10. These changes expand citations within existing background passages without substantially revising the research-positioning argument.

P1.justification: v3 shortens the opening motivation in Section 3.1, rewrites selected method explanations, updates consistency terminology, and changes author affiliations. Section ordering and most introductory, experimental, and appendix prose remain intact; much of the method rewriting accompanies substantive changes rather than document-wide restructuring.

P2.justification: Figure 1's caption replaces graph wavelet transformation with a spectral transform on graph signals. All four figure images and the table structures remain unchanged. Text and reference additions cause limited page reflow, without new displays or a substantial layout redesign.

improvement.justification: v3 adds useful implementation specificity, a scalable filtering option, and code-access information. However, substantial method revisions accompany identical experimental results without explaining which formulation produced them. Unchanged Figure 1 still specifies prediction consistency and omits the new regularizer, conflicting with the revised text. These documentation gains and unresolved method-to-evidence inconsistencies prevent a reliable net quality judgment.
